title: Offline bundle signing spec draft (working notes)
content:
Last updated: 2026-01-23 (Jordan)

This is a messy working draft spec for: Redwood Private offline bundle format + signing/verification.

Audience: installer/runtime engineers (Ethan), release eng (Connor/Sahana), security (Marcus/Kevin/Hanae), Solutions/Support (Fatima/Dev/Kira), SRE (Sean/Neha).

Status: Draft. Some sections are “notes to self” and open questions.

---

0. Why are we doing this (context)

Air-gapped customers want:
- No outbound network during install/upgrade (including “just to fetch a checksum”)
- Cryptographic integrity & provenance for everything installed
- A verification story that works fully offline (no OCSP/CT log assumptions)
- Audit evidence they can retain locally and optionally export

We currently ship “offline-ish” bundles but integrity/provenance is inconsistent (some pieces are checksummed, others not; signature story is incomplete; installer failure modes are not supportable).

Goal of this project (per PRD): a deterministic offline bundle, signed by Redwood, verified during installer preflight, fails closed by default, with policy-gated break-glass.

Non-goals (for now): customer-signed bundles / custom trust root as GA requirement. We should leave room to extend.

---

1. Terms (rough)

Bundle: A single distributable artifact (directory or tarball) that contains everything needed to install/upgrade Redwood Private in offline mode.

Manifest: Canonical metadata file inside the bundle enumerating required artifacts and cryptographic digests + versioning + build identifiers.

Signature: Cryptographic signature over a canonical representation of the manifest (and optionally other metadata). We should do detached signature file to keep manifest human-readable.

Trust store: Set of Redwood public signing keys that installer trusts (shipped with installer + optionally external override file).

Build ID: Unique identifier for a specific bundle build (ties to CI run / release metadata endpoint).

---

2. Bundle contents (bundle layout ideas)

NOTE: this section is still evolving; see also Confluence “offline-bundle-format-and-manifest”.

2.1 Proposed top-level layout

<bundle-root>/
  manifest.json                 (required)
  manifest.sig                  (required; detached signature)
  manifest.certchain.pem        (optional; only if we ship leaf+chain; TBD)
  sbom/
    bundle.spdx.json            (optional v1, likely required for GA) 
    bundle.spdx.json.sha256     (optional if included in manifest anyway)
  charts/
    redwood-private-<ver>.tgz
    redwood-private-<ver>.tgz.sha256 (maybe redundant; OK if referenced by manifest)
  images/
    index.json                  (list of images + digests)
    oci/
      <image tarballs OR registry mirror layout> (TBD: we likely have existing image packaging)
  artifacts/
    installer/
      redwood-private-installer-<ver>-linux-amd64
      redwood-private-installer-<ver>-linux-amd64.sha256
    runtime/
      <runtime blobs>
    models/
      <optional model artifacts> (NOTE: do we ship models in bundle or separately? customer-specific)
  docs/
    VERIFYING.md                (short guide for offline verification)
    CHANGELOG.md                (optional)
  metadata/
    build-info.json             (redundant but useful for quick inspection)

Open: do we want “bundle is a tar.gz” requirement? Some customers hate zip/unzip variability; tar.gz is more deterministic on Linux. But Windows transfer happens… We should at least document safe transfer + hashing before/after.

2.2 Bundle transport constraints (from customer convos)

Helios Defense:
- Bundle transported via approved removable media. They want a “single file” they can scan, then move. Strong preference: tarball.
- They want to run verification without installing anything (standalone “inspect” command).

AsterBank:
- They have strict “two-person rule” around installation media ingestion; they want printed or exportable verification report showing signer identity + hashes.
- They asked: “how do we know the signing key is controlled and rotated?”

GovLab Research:
- Procurement/legal wants a documented release process + evidence of key ceremony. They asked about “revocation” and how offline environments learn about it.

---

3. Manifest spec (draft)

3.1 File name + format
- File: manifest.json
- Encoding: UTF-8
- Canonicalization: MUST define ordering + whitespace rules. Proposal: JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS / RFC 8785). If we can’t adopt full RFC quickly, we must implement deterministic serialization ourselves and test it.

Notes:
- YAML is human-friendly but signature canonicalization is a footgun. Let’s stick with canonical JSON.

3.2 Manifest fields (v0 draft)

Top-level keys (draft):
- schema_version: "offline-bundle-manifest/v1" (string)
- bundle_version: e.g. "2026.01.0" (string, Redwood Private release)
- bundle_build_id: e.g. "priv-2026.01.0+build.18342" (string)
- created_at: ISO8601 timestamp, UTC (string)
- expires_at: optional, ISO8601 timestamp, UTC (string) (NOTE: controversial for air-gapped time skew)
- release_channel: "stable" | "rc" | "hotfix" (string)
- components: list of component entries (but remember: file must be flat JSON; still ok inside manifest itself; however this doc is describing it)
- signing:
  - algorithm: e.g. "ed25519" (string)
  - key_id: e.g. "redwood-release-ed25519-2025q4" (string)
  - signature_format: "detached" (string)
- downgrade_guard:
  - minimum_installer_version: e.g. "1.18.0" (string)
  - monotonic_release_number: integer as string? (e.g. "202601000") (string)

Each component entry includes:
- name: "installer" | "helm_charts" | "images" | "runtime" | "sbom" | etc.
- version: semantic-ish version string
- artifacts: list of artifacts entries with:
  - path: relative path within bundle
  - sha256: hex
  - size_bytes: integer (string)
  - type: "file" | "dir" (probably file only)

We also need:
- images index should reference OCI image digests (sha256:...) and optionally a tarball digest.
- chart tarball digest included.
- SBOM pointer: either inline SBOM artifact included + hashed, or path to SBOM + sha.

Open: do we need sha512? AsterBank asked “can you do sha512”; most accept sha256. Security likely OK w/ sha256.

3.3 Canonicalization requirements

Hard requirement: the bytes signed must be reproducible across build environments.

Proposal:
- canonical_json = RFC 8785 (JCS)
- signature = Sign(private_key, canonical_json_bytes)
- verify = Verify(public_key, canonical_json_bytes, signature_bytes)

We must avoid:
- Signing “pretty-printed JSON”
- Having different key ordering between languages

Test requirements (notes):
- golden test vectors: same manifest object serialized by Go, Python, JS should match canonical output (or at least verify signature)
- integration tests: tamper any byte in manifest -> verify fails

---

4. Signature envelope / files (draft)

4.1 Detached signature layout
- manifest.sig: base64-encoded signature OR a small JSON envelope.

Options:
A) Raw signature bytes base64
Pros: simple
Cons: no metadata (key_id, alg). You need to read manifest for that.

B) JSON envelope file:
{
  "schema_version": "offline-bundle-signature/v1",
  "algorithm": "ed25519",
  "key_id": "...",
  "signature": "base64...",
  "signed_file": "manifest.json",
  "signing_time": "..."
}
Pros: easier for tooling/support
Cons: we need to canonicalize envelope or keep envelope unsigned (but then metadata can be tampered). If envelope includes only redundant info also present in manifest, we can treat it as “informational”; actual trust is manifest+sig.

Current leaning (from ADR review thread): keep manifest authoritative; signature file can be raw base64 to reduce complexity.

4.2 Cert chain file?
If we use Ed25519 raw keys, no chain. If we use X.509 (e.g., ECDSA w/ certs), then we can include chain.

Customer notes: some security orgs like X.509 semantics, but offline revocation is hard. Ed25519 seems more straightforward for offline.

Need ADR-0147 final answer here; this doc should not diverge.

---

5. Trust model (draft)

5.1 Trust roots
Installer ships with:
- A trust store containing one or more Redwood public keys (key_id + public key bytes)
- Support for key rotation (multiple keys valid simultaneously)

Key rotation must not brick air-gapped environments. Practical constraints:
- They may not update installer frequently.
- They may stage bundles for weeks/months before install.

Therefore:
- Installer must allow multiple trusted keys.
- Redwood must publish “trust store update” artifact (also signed?) that customers can ingest offline.

Open: do we allow “external trust store file path”?
- Pros: air-gapped customers can update trust roots without replacing installer
- Cons: can be used to trust malicious keys if attackers control file
Mitigation: require policy gate / admin acknowledgment; log audit event.

5.2 Downgrade / replay
Threat model calls out replay of old signed bundles.

Possible controls:
- Include monotonic_release_number in manifest and store last-installed release number locally. Prevent installing older unless explicit rollback procedure.
- Include expires_at (but time in air-gap is messy; see time skew notes).

Leaning: downgrade protection based on local state + signed version metadata, not on time.

Open: rollback story needs to be documented: allow rollback to last-known-good if within allowed window? Might need a “rollback token” from admin? Probably too complex for v1.

---

6. Verification UX (installer + tooling)

6.1 Preflight
Installer command (proposed):
- redwood-private-installer preflight --bundle /path/to/bundle

Preflight steps:
1) locate manifest.json + manifest.sig
2) canonicalize manifest
3) verify signature against trust store
4) verify hashes for all referenced artifacts in manifest
5) verify required fields and versions (minimum_installer_version)
6) verify downgrade protection vs local install state
7) emit audit events locally
8) produce user-facing summary + machine-readable report (json)

Fail-closed: any signature failure -> exit non-zero and block install.

6.2 Inspect command (support / customer)
- redwood-private-installer bundle inspect --bundle ... [--verify]
Should print:
- bundle_version, build_id
- signer key_id
- signature status (OK/FAIL + reason)
- list of components + versions

Helios asked: “can we verify without root / without touching cluster?” => yes. Should be standalone.

6.3 Error taxonomy (notes)
We need stable error codes for Support.
Candidate buckets:
- SIGNATURE_MISSING
- SIGNATURE_INVALID
- KEY_UNTRUSTED
- MANIFEST_INVALID_SCHEMA
- HASH_MISMATCH
- ARTIFACT_MISSING
- DOWNGRADE_BLOCKED
- TIME_SKEW_SUSPECTED (if we keep time validity; TBD)
- BREAK_GLASS_USED (not an error, but audit marker)

This ties to Slack thread: eng-platform/1760510044-installer-verification-error-taxonomy.

---

7. Break-glass (ugh but required)

Principles:
- Break-glass must be explicit and noisy.
- Must be policy gated (RBAC / config). Not just a hidden flag.
- Must leave audit evidence (local log + “marker file” + support bundle inclusion).

Candidate CLI:
- redwood-private-installer install --bundle ... --allow-unsigned-bundle
or
- --skip-bundle-verification (preferred wording: avoid “skip security”)

Security requirement (Marcus): break-glass usage should require a second step / typed acknowledgment OR config file enabling it.

Operational requirement (Sean): support must be able to detect break-glass was used when troubleshooting.

Open questions:
- Do we allow break-glass for “unknown key” only, but not for “invalid signature”? I think policy should allow for emergency but require approvals.
- Do we allow break-glass in GA? PRD implies yes but with strict procedure.

---

8. Build + signing pipeline (release eng notes)

Deterministic build:
- Given the same inputs, produce same manifest and artifact hashes.
- Avoid embedding timestamps in binaries that become part of hash unless intentionally tracked.

Signing step:
- Must run in protected CI environment.
- Keys stored in HSM/KMS with access controls. Separation of duties.

Evidence:
- Capture who approved signing, when, what commit/release tag, and the resulting signature.
- Save logs for compliance evidence mapping.

Connor/Sahana requested:
- gating check: Private release cannot ship if signed bundle missing or verification tests failed.

See: Linear ENG-4822 and ENG-4862.

---

9. SBOM requirements (draft)

We likely need at least a bundle-level SBOM artifact included in bundle and referenced by manifest.

Notes:
- AsterBank asked: “Does SBOM cover the container images?” -> ideally yes; at minimum, include image digest list. SBOM generation might lag but we can include pointer.

Open: is SBOM “required” for v1 pilot or GA? PRD says pointer in manifest (PR-24918).

---

10. Audit logging (private deployment)

We must emit verification outcome events locally.

Minimal events:
- bundle_verification_started
- bundle_verification_succeeded
- bundle_verification_failed (include reason code)
- break_glass_override_used

Fields to include (draft, do not over-collect):
- timestamp (local)
- bundle_build_id
- bundle_version
- key_id (signer)
- verification_result
- failure_code (if any)
- installer_version
- host_id or node_id (careful: privacy / customer policies)

Export:
- If audit log exporter configured, map events to SIEM schema.

Kevin Osei to confirm schema mapping; Logan Wright to implement emission path.

---

11. Handling time in air-gapped environments

This keeps coming up. If we add cert validity windows or signature “not before/after” we risk bricking installs due to time skew.

Customer constraints:
- Many air-gapped envs do not have reliable NTP.
- They sometimes intentionally keep systems “behind” due to patching cycles.

Proposal:
- Avoid time-based validation for signature (Ed25519 signature itself has no time).
- If we include created_at, treat as informational.
- If we include expires_at, do not hard-fail on it in v1; maybe warn.

BUT: Security may want expiration to limit blast radius for key compromise.

Open: can we do expiration in the “trust store” rather than per-bundle? Example: trust store includes key validity. Still time-based though.

Action: review threat model recommendation; decide in ADR.

---

12. Compatibility / migration

Migration from unsigned bundles:
- Existing customers may have existing installer versions.
- We need a transition period where installer can accept unsigned bundles only if configured (or for older release lines).

Possible approach:
- Start producing signed bundles for a given Private release (2026.01?)
- Require minimum installer version for those bundles.
- Provide a migration guide + explicit messaging.

Open: Should installer default to “require signed” always, even for older bundles? That may break existing customers.

Downgrade: prevent accidental downgrade by default.
Rollback: allow rollback with explicit procedure. (Need separate doc.)

---

13. Notes from specific customer conversations (raw)

13.1 Helios Defense (2025-10-14 deep dive)
- They want a deterministic “single artifact” to move across security zones.
- They will run an internal scanning tool on the tarball; they want to verify signature before scan too.
- They asked: “If our installer is outdated, can we still verify the bundle?” => prefer yes via inspect tool shipped with bundle OR standalone verifier binary.
  - Counterpoint: shipping verifier inside the bundle is circular trust unless verifier is also signed by an already trusted key (or verified via OS trust). But could be ok if they trust installer distribution channel.
- They want printed report of hashes for chain-of-custody. (We can generate report from manifest.)

13.2 AsterBank (2025-10-22 security review)
- Key custody: they asked who can sign releases, where keys live, how often rotated.
- Audit logs: need local logging with retention guidance. Export is optional but must exist.
- They asked about “revocation”: how do they know a key is revoked if offline? Answer likely: trust store update + out-of-band notification.

13.3 GovLab Research (2026-01-09 procurement/legal)
- Wants documented policy: what is signed, how, approvals, and evidence (key ceremony).
- Wants contractual language referencing “signed release artifacts.” (Product to handle.)

---

14. Open questions / TODOs (keep this list short but real)

Crypto / format
- Decide alg/key format: Ed25519 raw keys vs ECDSA/X.509. (ADR-0147 should settle; align doc.)
- Decide signature file format: raw base64 vs JSON envelope.
- Decide whether we sign only manifest or also include signature over “bundle root listing” (manifest already includes artifacts). Probably manifest only.

Bundle structure
- Single tarball requirement? Or allow directory layout? (Support headaches.)
- Do we support Windows unzip tools? We saw corruption issues (line endings) in some transfers.

Trust store
- How do customers update trust store offline without installer update? External trust file vs separate signed trust bundle.
- How do we communicate revocation? What’s the SLA?

Downgrade / rollback
- Decide downgrade prevention mechanism and supported rollback story. Need compatibility matrix.

Time
- Do we ever hard-fail due to “expired signature”? If yes, how do we handle time skew safely?

Docs / enablement
- Provide quick verification guide: commands + expected output.
- Provide Support runbook for common failures (hash mismatch, unknown key, invalid sig).

---

15. Next steps (as of last edit)

- Jordan: incorporate decisions from ADR-0147; update manifest schema section accordingly.
- Ethan: align installer preflight flow + error codes with Support (Dev Patel) and docs (Kira).
- Connor/Sahana: define signing pipeline gating checks and test artifacts.
- Marcus/Kevin: confirm threat model requirements for key rotation, downgrade protection, and audit evidence.
- Fatima: validate “inspect without install” requirement with pilots; confirm whether they can update installer easily.

End of draft.
